issues.description: The problem statement (UML and textual description) specifies acceptSupplyDelivery should take four parameters (supplier name, ingredient name, price, quantity) — signature acceptSupplyDelivery(String, String, int, int) — but both the provided template usage and the solution implement and call acceptSupplyDelivery with three parameters (ingredient name, price, quantity) as acceptSupplyDelivery(String, int, int). This mismatch between the specification and the code will confuse students about the required method signature and parameter meaning.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the specification and code consistent. Either (A) update the problem statement (UML and text) to state acceptSupplyDelivery(String ingredientName, int price, int quantity) (three parameters) to match the template and solution, or (B) change the template and solution to implement acceptSupplyDelivery(String supplierName, String ingredientName, int price, int quantity) and update all call sites accordingly. Prefer updating the problem statement to the three-parameter form if supplier name is not used in the exercise logic.

issues.description: The problem statement UML and description specify acceptSupplyDelivery with four parameters (supplierName, ingredientName, price, quantity) i.e. acceptSupplyDelivery(String, String, int, int), but both the template example calls (Main) and the solution implement acceptSupplyDelivery with three parameters (ingredientName, price, quantity) i.e. acceptSupplyDelivery(String, int, int). This mismatch in the method signature (presence/absence of the supplier String parameter) creates confusion for students about the required method contract and which parameters to implement/use.
issues.suggestedFix: Align the specification and the code. Either (A) update the problem statement/UML to specify acceptSupplyDelivery(String ingredientName, int price, int quantity) (remove the supplier parameter), or (B) update the template and solution to implement acceptSupplyDelivery(String supplierName, String ingredientName, int price, int quantity) and change all call sites (e.g., Main) accordingly. This ensures a single, consistent method signature across problem, template, and solution.
